bugs.name: Global /pulls with sort=newest is ordered like Recently updated
bugs.summary: With Sort = Newest the rows are not in creation order: in the screenshot 'agent2: add compare notes file' (opened 2 minutes ago) is listed above 'Add agent3-rebase-notes.md' (opened 1 minute ago). Verified against the exact timestamps in the page: order was 15:33:27, 15:31:29, 15:33:02, 15:30:40, 15:30:20, 15:30:30, 15:30:17, 15:28:38, 15:29:51, 15:28:36, 15:28:22 — not descending. The same data under Sort = Oldest is perfectly ascending (15:28:22 … 15:33:27), and the Newest order is identical to Sort = Recently updated, so Newest appears to ignore creation time and sort by last update. (on /pulls)
bugs.expected: Sort > Newest should list pull requests by creation time, most recently opened first (the exact reverse of Sort > Oldest, which is correctly ordered by creation time ascending).
bugs.actual: With Sort = Newest the rows are not in creation order: in the screenshot 'agent2: add compare notes file' (opened 2 minutes ago) is listed above 'Add agent3-rebase-notes.md' (opened 1 minute ago). Verified against the exact timestamps in the page: order was 15:33:27, 15:31:29, 15:33:02, 15:30:40, 15:30:20, 15:30:30, 15:30:17, 15:28:38, 15:29:51, 15:28:36, 15:28:22 — not descending. The same data under Sort = Oldest is perfectly ascending (15:28:22 … 15:33:27), and the Newest order is identical to Sort = Recently updated, so Newest appears to ignore creation time and sort by last update.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval (password momentic-eval-1) and open https://5503-iotjkrbhq2ztebrw6o97y.e2b.app/pulls?type=your_repositories&sort=newest&state=open (or open /pulls, click 'Pull Requests' in the global navigation and choose Sort > Newest)
Read the 'opened … ago' line under each pull request title down the list
Compare with the same list opened as https://5503-iotjkrbhq2ztebrw6o97y.e2b.app/pulls?type=your_repositories&sort=oldest&state=open
bugs.reason: The reported address uses sort=newest, a value the page never produces: the Sort > Newest link sends sort=latest, which maps to creation time descending, and any unknown value falls back to updated-descending, exactly the order seen. No screenshot or frame shows the menu being used, so the claim about the UI path is not shown.

bugs.name: Changing a pull request's target branch re-creates the 'added 1 commit' event at the end of the timeline with a new time
bugs.summary: After the two base-branch changes the timeline ends with "eval changed target branch from main to agent4-base-branch 1 minute ago", "eval changed target branch from agent4-base-branch to main now" and then "eval added 1 commit now / agent4: reopen test file ab6a366877", while "eval commented 15 minutes ago" stays at the top — the commit that was pushed 16 minutes earlier is re-stamped "now" and pulled out of its chronological place in the timeline. (on /eval/harbor-handbook/pulls/18)
bugs.expected: Changing the target branch should only add a "changed target branch" event; the existing "added 1 commit" event keeps its original position in the timeline (right after the description, before the close/reopen and branch-change events) and its original time.
bugs.actual: After the two base-branch changes the timeline ends with "eval changed target branch from main to agent4-base-branch 1 minute ago", "eval changed target branch from agent4-base-branch to main now" and then "eval added 1 commit now / agent4: reopen test file ab6a366877", while "eval commented 15 minutes ago" stays at the top — the commit that was pushed 16 minutes earlier is re-stamped "now" and pulled out of its chronological place in the timeline.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and open https://5503-iotjkrbhq2ztebrw6o97y.e2b.app/eval/harbor-handbook/pulls/18 (agent4-reopen-flow PR) and note the timeline order: the "added 1 commit" event sits directly under the description, before the close/reopen events.
Press the "Edit" button at the top right of the pull request.
In the edit bar open the "merge into: eval:main" dropdown and choose "eval:agent4-base-branch" (a branch created from main with one extra file), then press "Save".
Press "Edit" again, open the "merge into" dropdown, choose "eval:main", press "Save".
Scroll through the Conversation timeline and read the last three events.
bugs.reason: Deliberate: when the target branch changes, the code deletes every push event of the pull request and creates a fresh one against the new base ('Delete all old push comments and insert new push comments'), because the set of commits in the pull request depends on the base.

bugs.name: Author filter on the global pull request list keeps the label 'Author' and shows the chosen user only as prefilled search text
bugs.summary: The Author control still reads just 'Author' with no user shown, so nothing on the page tells the person the list is filtered by alex (only 'opened by alex' in the row hints at it). Reopening the dropdown shows the search box prefilled with 'alex' but no alex row to see or unselect — only 'All users' — so the active filter cannot be seen or cleared by name. Seen twice: right after choosing alex, and after a reload. (on /pulls)
bugs.expected: The Author filter shows the selected user in the dropdown (like the Sort control shows the active order) and, when reopened, lists that user as the current selection so it can be seen and cleared.
bugs.actual: The Author control still reads just 'Author' with no user shown, so nothing on the page tells the person the list is filtered by alex (only 'opened by alex' in the row hints at it). Reopening the dropdown shows the search box prefilled with 'alex' but no alex row to see or unselect — only 'All users' — so the active filter cannot be seen or cleared by name. Seen twice: right after choosing alex, and after a reload.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and open https://5503-iyhuwnqi1q5k6kqzc08au.e2b.app/pulls
Click the 'Author' dropdown above the list
Type 'alex' in its 'Search users' box and click the 'alex' option
The list is now filtered to alex's pull request (#25) and the address ends with &poster=alex
Look at the Author control: it still reads 'Author'; click it again — the search box holds 'alex' but no alex row is offered, only 'All users'
bugs.reason: By design: the control always prints its fixed title, and the script puts the selected username into the search box when the menu opens; 'All users' clears it. The source also notes this page has no user list to offer and takes usernames directly, so a missing 'alex' row is the stated limitation, not a failure, and the filter can be both seen and cleared.

bugs.name: Dashboard sidebar counters ('In your repositories', 'Created by you') do not follow the Author filter

The same sidebar does follow the search box (a search that matches nothing shows 'In your repositories 0'), so the counter contradicts the list it sits next to. (on /org/harbor14/pulls)
bugs.expected: The sidebar counter should match the filtered list (0), as the Open/Closed tab already does, since the page presents the counter as the number of pull requests in the current result set.
bugs.actual: The list shows 'No results' and the tab says '0 Open / 0 Closed', but the sidebar still says 'In your repositories 5' and 'Created by you 5'. The same sidebar does follow the search box (a search that matches nothing shows 'In your repositories 0'), so the counter contradicts the list it sits next to.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval / momentic-eval-1 and open https://5503-iyhuwnqi1q5k6kqzc08au.e2b.app/org/harbor14/pulls (the org has 5 open PRs, all opened by eval).
Click 'Author', type 'alex' in 'Search users' and pick the user alex.

Read the page: the result area says 'No results / Try adjusting your search filters.' and the tab reads '0 Open 0 Closed', but the left column still reads 'In your repositories 5' and 'Created by you 5'.

bugs.name: After signing out, the browser Back button shows the previously viewed private pull request pages
bugs.summary: Both earlier pages come back from the browser's back-forward cache exactly as they were before signing out: the top-right still shows the signed-in eval avatar instead of "Sign In", the PR conversation still shows "Owner", "Edit", the merge box with "Update branch by merge" and the comment editor, and the Files tab still shows the full diff of all 3 files with "1 / 3 files viewed" and the Review button. Only a reload shows the truth — it redirects to /user/login, proving the session is gone and the pages are private-repository content. (on /eval/harbor-handbook/pulls/16)
bugs.expected: After signing out, Back should not show the private repository's pull request pages with the signed-in header and working-looking controls; the person should get the sign-in page (or a clearly anonymous, read-only view) instead of cached authenticated content.
bugs.actual: Both earlier pages come back from the browser's back-forward cache exactly as they were before signing out: the top-right still shows the signed-in eval avatar instead of "Sign In", the PR conversation still shows "Owner", "Edit", the merge box with "Update branch by merge" and the comment editor, and the Files tab still shows the full diff of all 3 files with "1 / 3 files viewed" and the Review button. Only a reload shows the truth — it redirects to /user/login, proving the session is gone and the pages are private-repository content.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval / momentic-eval-1 and open https://5503-i6dtbtklp3c8hdj643mx8.e2b.app/eval/harbor-handbook/pulls/16 (also visit its Files Changed tab /files).
Open the avatar menu at the top right and click "Sign Out": the site returns to the signed-out home page.
Press the browser's Back button once: the pull request conversation /16 comes back fully rendered with the signed-in header, Owner badge, Edit button, merge box and comment editor.
Press Back again: the /16/files tab also comes back fully rendered with its diff and Review button. Reloading that address then redirects to /user/login.
bugs.reason: This is the browser redisplaying pages it already had; no new data is served and a reload goes to the sign-in page. The source states the choice on purpose: pages are sent with 'max-age=0, private, must-revalidate' instead of 'no-store' so that browsers can restore form input when navigating back.
